metadata.title: Global Sanctions Source Registry
metadata.scope: Financial, trade, travel and transport sanctions; export controls; relevant enforcement; separately classified adjacent/reference sources
methodology: This is a global source catalogue for an open-source reporting dashboard, organized by publishing jurisdiction. It is not a dataset of sanctioned entities or a feed of actual events.

The country baseline is 193 UN members plus Holy See and Palestine. Eighteen additional jurisdictions are listed separately. Country inclusion does not assert that an autonomous regime or public consolidated list exists.

Official source verified means the official publication, official indexed content or documented official linkage and sanctions relevance were identified. It does not mean every URL was fetched successfully or every linked download was tested.

Official institutional entry only means an official ministry, regulator or FIU entry point was found, but no dedicated sanctions-specific publication/feed was established. These rows have regime_basis=unknown.
Published formats describe observed or publisher-advertised formats. All production connectors, endpoint reliability, pagination, refresh latency and historical completeness remain untested.
Rows may be hubs, lists, legal instruments, notices, guidance, historical examples or enforcement channels. Date and scope caveats in each row must be preserved.

The same legal action may appear in UN/EU sources, national republications, newsrooms and aggregators. Retain original issuer, publisher, legal identifier and timestamps to deduplicate events without deleting distinct national implementing measures.
Procurement debarment, FATF country-risk statements, maritime reference data, intelligence reporting and de facto notices must not be converted into government asset-freeze designations.

The 25-concept lexicon is authored seed vocabulary in eight languages. It is not an evaluated classifier or certified legal translation. Official conceptual evidence does not certify each translated phrase.
The event dictionary specifies 45 proposed fields; it is not an executable JSON Schema or an implemented extraction pipeline. Its examples are illustrative placeholders, not actual events.
Source and content reuse terms have not been comprehensively reviewed. Public accessibility and open-source dashboard code do not establish unrestricted redistribution rights.

Coverage does not claim every court, prosecutor, customs branch, local implementation notice, historical measure or separate territory in the world. The coverage checklist and caveats make the remaining research work explicit.

metadata.region_convention: UN Statistics Division M49 broad geographic regions (Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, Oceania). These are geographic reporting groups rather than the research assignment groups or political alignments. Cyprus, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Kazakhstan and Türkiye are in Asia; the Russian Federation is in Europe.
metadata.name_convention: canonical_name and un_name reproduce the UN M49 English short country name retrieved on the as_of date. display_name uses familiar short names where useful. NR is shown as Naoero (Nauru), with Nauru retained as an alias; the current official UN membership and M49 pages use Naoero.

topic_map.title: Sanctions regimes, designations and legal changes
topic_map.description: Regime creation/change, country or sector restrictions, additions/removals/amendments and permitted exceptions.

suggested_official_authorities.role: National/UN TFS implementation and list changes.

distinctions: A targeted country is not the issuer jurisdiction.
UN or foreign list republication does not create another autonomous designation.
Name lists alone omit sectoral and activity-based restrictions.
Official acts, effective dates, exceptions and applicable jurisdiction determine legal effect.
Domestic terrorist labels must remain attributed to the designating government.

topic_map.title: Sanctioned vessels and shadow-fleet reporting
topic_map.description: Legally designated/specified ships, registry action and separately attributed intelligence or risk reporting about maritime networks.

suggested_official_authorities.role: Official designation records and vessel identifiers.
Current UK designated persons and specified/designated ship records.
Vessel restrictions, port access, detention and movement powers.
Official intelligence reporting on ships, networks and proposed targets; not itself proof of legal designation.
Delegated flag administrator's marine advisories and registry conditions.

distinctions: A shadow-fleet label or intelligence portal entry is not automatically a legally effective ship designation.
IMO identifies the ship more persistently than name, flag or MMSI; preserve identity history and explicit matches.
An ownership or management link does not establish identical legal restrictions without the applicable control rules.
Separate intended routes, authority-reported movements and independently observed movements.
HOCC/Sana’a de facto notices, if monitored, belong in a separate attributed maritime-risk layer, not national Yemen or UN sanctions.

topic_map.title: Oil, petroleum products and maritime-services restrictions
topic_map.description: Oil trade prohibitions, price-cap services rules, conditional permissions and registry implementation.

suggested_official_authorities.role: Oil price-cap and maritime-services guidance.
Licences, reporting forms and changes.
Jurisdiction-specific oil/energy programme measures.
Binding prohibitions, product annexes and amendments.
Dated December 2025 registry advisory on Russian-oil voyage attestations and flag conditions; check later updates.

distinctions: Record product, origin, transaction date, jurisdiction and services scope; caps and permissions can change.
Cargo origin is different from loading port, transit route or ship flag.
Oil transported by a listed or high-risk ship is not automatically evidence of a particular breach.
A price-cap attestation is a compliance document, not independent proof of price or lawful conduct.
A registry operational condition is distinct from the underlying US, UK or EU restriction.

topic_map.title: Dual-use goods, technology and proliferation controls
topic_map.description: Controlled civilian goods or technology, end-user/end-use controls and licensing.

suggested_official_authorities.role: End-user, end-use and US-person restrictions with links to distinct screening lists.

suggested_official_authorities.authority: Executive Office for Control and Non-Proliferation
suggested_official_authorities.role: Controlled strategic goods and dual-use chemicals.

suggested_official_authorities.authority: Council for the Non-Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction
suggested_official_authorities.role: Controlled goods, notices and permits.
Civil dual-use export licensing framework.

distinctions: Export-control list status is distinct from an asset freeze or travel ban.
Keep HS/CN customs codes, ECCNs and national control-list entries separate; no one-to-one mapping is assumed.
Control may depend on technology specifications, end use, end user, destination and jurisdiction.
A commercial product description alone does not establish a controlled classification.
Track software, technical assistance and technology-transfer restrictions when the cited instrument covers them.

topic_map.title: Arms embargoes and defence trade
topic_map.description: Arms transfers, military-list controls, restricted destinations/end users and embargo exemptions.

suggested_official_authorities.role: Embargo resolutions, committees and relevant exemptions.

suggested_official_authorities.authority: State Department Directorate of Defense Trade Controls
suggested_official_authorities.role: Defence trade controls, debarment and enforcement information.
Defence export controls and UN embargo references.
Embargo decisions/regulations and national implementation references.

distinctions: Embargo scope, direction, targeted recipients, goods and exemptions must come from the instrument.
An arms embargo does not automatically prohibit all civilian exports or all transactions with a country.
Distinguish authorised transfers, alleged violations, official interdictions and final judicial findings.
Military goods controls and civilian dual-use controls can overlap but retain distinct classification schemes.

topic_map.title: Luxury goods restrictions
topic_map.description: Regime-specific restrictions on goods classified as luxury items, with listed categories and any value thresholds.

suggested_official_authorities.role: Product annexes, customs classifications, thresholds and amendments.
Trade-sanctions guidance, licences and enforcement updates.
Export restriction framework and applicable regulatory references.
Official trade/customs investigations and seizures where a sanctions nexus is established.

distinctions: Luxury is a legal category in a particular regime, not a universal label or price rule.
Product codes, unit-value thresholds, valuation basis, origin/destination and exceptions must be sourced.
A luxury yacht designation concerns the ship/owner and does not automatically mean a luxury-goods export violation.
Counterfeiting, customs duties and ordinary import infringements should not be labelled sanctions violations without evidence.

topic_map.title: Sanctions evasion networks and risk indicators
topic_map.description: Officially reported ownership networks, concealment methods, suspicious trade and maritime indicators.

suggested_official_authorities.role: Official alert on shadow-fleet sanctions evasion/avoidance networks.
Maritime typologies and due-diligence indicators.

suggested_official_authorities.authority: Department of Justice National Security Division
suggested_official_authorities.role: Sanctions/export-control investigations, charges and case outcomes.
Attributed designation narratives and alleged network roles.

distinctions: AIS gaps, ship-to-ship transfers, flag changes and complex ownership are risk indicators, not standalone proof of illegality.
Preserve the authority making each allegation and distinguish charges from admissions or judgments.
Separate direct source-supported network links from analyst inference; record evidence for each relationship.
Do not double-count coordinated notices or infer joint liability solely from a shared address, manager or transaction.

topic_map.title: Freezes, seizures, detentions, forfeitures and prosecutions
topic_map.description: Enforcement events and their procedural outcomes, linked to the applicable sanctions or export-control nexus.

suggested_official_authorities.authority: Department of Justice National Security Division
suggested_official_authorities.role: Criminal enforcement, seizure/forfeiture cases and judgments.
Civil penalties, settlements and enforcement findings.
Financial-sanctions enforcement decisions.
Customs enforcement announcements; most releases require sanctions-relevance filtering.

suggested_official_authorities.authority: National Bureau for Counter Terror Financing
suggested_official_authorities.role: Official seizure orders.

distinctions: An asset freeze restricts dealing; seizure concerns control/custody; forfeiture or confiscation reflects a distinct legal deprivation as defined by the applicable order.
Detention of a ship or consignment is not automatically confiscation or proof of a sanctions breach.
A prosecution is an allegation until the applicable adjudicative outcome; record acquittal, dismissal, release and reversal.
A penalty or settlement is not another designation, and settlement language may contain no admission.
Ordinary drug seizures, customs offences and AML administrative penalties require an explicit sanctions/export-control connection before inclusion.

event_field_dictionary.description: Stable local identifier for one atomic event; repeated publications do not create another underlying action.
Identifier linking the publication to the source registry; an illustrative placeholder here.
Body that legally issues the action or makes the attributed assertion. This can differ from the website publishing it; use null if unresolved.
Body operating the source publication, including a regulator republishing another issuer's list.
Jurisdiction or intergovernmental body responsible for the action. Preserve institutional scope; UN/EU and de facto authorities must not be forced into sovereign ISO codes.
Jurisdiction of the publishing institution. Local republication does not change the issuer or establish another autonomous sanction.
Canonical primary publication URL for the event, preferably the specific notice or legal instrument rather than its agency homepage.
Publication date or timestamp as stated by the publisher. Retain available precision and timezone; null when unavailable, with no fabricated midnight.
UTC timestamp when the publication was actually retrieved; distinct from publication, event and effective dates.
Language of the source text; preserve original text alongside any separately attributed translation.
Digest of archived original bytes, with algorithm and byte scope. A hash proves captured-content integrity, not truth or current legal validity.
Date or timestamp of the reported action or occurrence, such as a seizure. May precede publication; do not substitute the publication date.

One atomic action: designation, removal, amendment, asset_freeze, seizure, forfeiture, detention, release, investigation, prosecution, conviction, acquittal, civil_penalty, licence, exemption, trade_restriction, guidance, or other. Store separate linked events when a notice reports several. Freeze, seizure, forfeiture, detention and prosecution are not interchangeable.

Exact act, regulation, resolution, order, court case or official decision authorising or recording the event; include citation and operative provision. A press release is not automatically the operative instrument.

Applicable sanctions/export-control regimes, official programme codes and legal nexus, supported by source evidence. Empty means not established, not no applicable regime; retain multiple regimes without merging their legal effects.

Procedural/execution status: proposed, announced, ordered, filed, ongoing, implemented, resolved, cancelled, or unknown. Prosecution filed is not conviction; an announced freeze is not evidence of execution.

Current status of the legal measure: in_force, stayed, suspended, expired, revoked, annulled, not_applicable, or unknown. Default unknown; date or old list presence alone does not prove continuing validity.
Commencement of legal effect, including delayed commencement where stated; null if unverified. Never assume it equals publication.
Stated expiry or end of legal effect; null means unknown or unstated, not necessarily indefinite.

autonomous_national, UN_action, UN_implementation, EU_action, EU_implementation, foreign_republication, delegated_registry_condition, de_facto_notice, other, or unknown. Record domestic terrorism designations as issuer actions; distinguish legal obligations from advisory republication.

Operative restrictions or permissions, with affected activities, exceptions and conditions. Examples include asset freeze, travel ban, arms embargo, port ban, services prohibition and conditional licence; a designation does not imply every measure.

event_field_dictionary.description: Primary subject: person, organisation, vessel, aircraft, goods, state, sector, or other. Broad policy events may have no individually named subject.
Names and aliases exactly as sourced, retaining original scripts, transliterations and source attribution; a fuzzy name match is not an identity determination.

Identifiers with scheme, issuing body/jurisdiction and validity dates where known: official list ID, company number, LEI, passport, aircraft registration, etc. Do not treat all numbers as equivalent or expose unnecessary personal details.

Evidence-backed ownership, control, operator, manager, beneficial-owner or other links. Include percentage/date if stated and distinguish allegation from established relationship; do not infer automatic sanctions coverage merely from a link.
Original description of cargo, equipment, commodity or goods. Preserve qualifiers and uncertainty; a generic oil/electronics/luxury label does not establish legal control.
event_field_dictionary.example: Illustrative industrial electronic components; precise model not reported

event_field_dictionary.description: Keep HS, CN, TARIC, ECCN, national export-control and military-list schemes distinct, with version, code and authority/source. Leave unresolved codes absent; never infer an ECCN or sanctions coverage from an HS/CN code alone.
Reported quantities, weights, volumes and valuations with units, currency, valuation basis and date. Distinguish seized amount, cargo value and penalty; never silently convert or equate them.

Seven-digit IMO ship identification number when explicitly sourced; validate format/check digit and attribution. It generally follows the ship across name/flag changes, unlike MMSI. Do not manufacture an IMO for an unnumbered vessel.
MMSI radio identifiers as nine-digit strings with source and observation dates. MMSI can change with flag/radio registration or be spoofed; it is not a permanent hull identifier.
Vessel names and claimed/registered flags at relevant dates; preserve historical values and identify the registry or source. Do not assign today's flag to a past event.
Event, asset or cargo locations with type, jurisdiction and optional coordinates/accuracy; distinguish a report's dateline from the actual event location.
Port references with role and verified UN/LOCODE when available. A name is not a verified code; store code-list version and do not confuse an intended port with a completed call.

Separate observed, issuer_reported, third_party_reported, inferred and intended route segments. Record endpoints, times, evidence, gaps and uncertainty; never connect missing AIS points into a proven route or treat an intended destination as arrival.

example.gaps: No independent tracking data in source

event_field_dictionary.description: Reported loading, discharge, ship-to-ship transfer, port call, flag change, AIS anomaly or other activity with time and evidence status. Activity or risk indicator alone does not establish a designation or breach.

Epistemic/legal status of the conduct asserted: allegation, issuer_asserted, admitted, judicial_finding, independently_corroborated, contested, or unknown. Designation is an administrative legal event, not by itself a conviction or proof of its stated conduct.
Who asserts the conduct and in what capacity; preserve materially conflicting accounts separately. An official source establishes what the authority says, not automatic independent confirmation.

example.statement: Alleged conduct as described in the source

event_field_dictionary.description: Evidence supporting individual fields/claims, including URL, document/page/paragraph or short excerpt, retrieved time and optional content hash. Capture operative legal text and corroboration separately; use minimal compliant excerpts.

Status of this event record: official_primary_verified, official_primary_partially_accessible, corroborated, single_source_unverified, disputed, or unknown. This tests provenance/claims, independently of current legal validity.
Human-readable gaps, translation issues, access restrictions, conflicting data or reasons a conclusion remains unknown. Do not replace explicit structured statuses with a confidence score.
event_field_dictionary.example: Official release verified; operative court order and current validity have not been verified.

event_field_dictionary.description: Canonical event to which this publication is a true duplicate, including local republications and translations. Same subject or similar date alone is insufficient; distinct national implementation decisions are separate events.

Links to genuinely distinct events in a sequence: designation, subsequent freeze, seizure, prosecution, judgment, release or delisting. Include relationship type rather than collapsing them into one status.
Earlier event or version explicitly amended/replaced by this event; preserve history and the scope of amendment. A document update need not mean the whole prior measure is revoked.
Time when current legal validity or latest procedural outcome was actually checked against an appropriate authoritative source; null if no such check was completed.
How this record was produced: manual/rule/model, parser/model version and reviewer/review date if used. Extraction confidence is not legal certainty.
